Tests full requested→resolved state transition.; test_repeated_claim_requests_reuse_the_pending_row: Repeats the same pending claim request and asserts identical row ID and only one DB claim; guards retries from queue duplication.; test_claiming_a_held_credit_is_rejected: After account 1 owns `Player`, account 2 requesting it raises `AliasAlreadyClaimedError`; creator credit cannot be reassigned through claim request.; test_claim_request_for_an_uncredited_name_is_rejected: Request for absent alias `NeverCredited` raises `CreatorAliasNotFoundError`; distinguishes uncredited identity from an existing unclaimed credit.; test_public_creator_redirect_resolves_to_the_surviving_profile: Inserts retired public UUID redirect to claimant and resolves it; response keeps requested retired ID, reports canonical ID, and shows alias. This is public URL compatibility after merge.

test_orm_insert_writes_the_fold: ORM insert of whitespace-wrapped Greek sigmas persists normalized `σσ`; verifies declared SQLAlchemy default performs Python casefold, not SQL lower.; test_core_on_conflict_insert_writes_the_fold: PostgreSQL Core `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` of full-width Alice persists `alice`; build submission uses this non-ORM path, so ORM coverage cannot replace it.; test_executemany_writes_the_fold: Bulk insert folds ligature `ﬁx` and whitespace-wrapped Bob to `fix`/`bob`; covers SQLAlchemy executemany defaults separately from single insert.; test_updating_the_name_refolds: ORM rename `Bob`→`Straße` stores `strasse`; directly exercises `_refold_on_name_change` because global `onupdate` would also refold unrelated claim updates.; test_check_constraint_rejects_an_unfolded_raw_write: Raw SQL explicitly writes name/fold both `Bob`; named DB CHECK rejects writers bypassing SQLAlchemy folding default, the final guard distinct from ORM/Core folding tests.; test_names_that_only_casefold_unifies_are_one_creator: Seeds `ΣΣ`, then rejects `Σς` at normalized unique key and resolves all three spellings back to original alias; tests non-ASCII fold consistently through insertion, lookup and uniqueness.; test_dotted_capital_i_stays_a_distinct_creator: Stores `İ` and `I` together; resulting keys are `i`+combining dot versus plain `i`, ensuring Unicode casefold does not over-collapse distinct names.

test_reserving_previews_the_java_identity: Valid code reservation yields exact UUID/name, no credit, no existing owner, live expiry/token; read-only consent preview data differs from redemption outcomes tested below.; test_reserving_does_not_spend_the_code: Reserve, create account only after prompt, redeem with matching token; result has account+refresh, showing preview hold is not itself consumption.; test_a_held_code_cannot_be_reserved_twice: After first live hold, immediate second reservation returns None; sequential token exclusivity distinct from concurrency case.; test_concurrent_reservations_issue_exactly_one_hold: Two simultaneous reservation calls on same valid code return two result slots but exactly one non-None token; checks row-lock/conditional hold race.; test_releasing_frees_the_code_immediately: Releasing the exact token returns true and makes same code reservable at once; tests explicit early release rather than waiting for expiration.; test_releasing_is_idempotent_and_ignores_a_foreign_token: Foreign token cannot clear hold; matching token clears once, second release returns false. Covers absent and consumed states; live-held/expired reservation cases are separate.

test_a_ticket_round_trips_and_is_spent_once: Mint, peek and consume CODE1234; first consume succeeds and replay returns None, distinguishing non-consuming preview from one-shot redemption.; test_the_plaintext_code_is_never_stored: Queries stored digest after minting CODE1234; no digest equals or contains plaintext, guarding leaked merge bearer secret.; test_minting_replaces_the_accounts_live_ticket: Mints FIRST then SECOND; only second peeks successfully and one ticket row remains, so old account code is revoked immediately.; test_a_ticket_cannot_be_minted_already_expired: Negative TTL ticket insert violates DB CHECK and raises IntegrityError; application-side positive TTL checks alone cannot protect direct storage.; test_an_expired_ticket_stops_matching: A row aged consistently to past expiry remains stored but neither peek nor consume matches; storage cleanup is not required for access control.; test_a_ticket_needs_a_real_account: Ticket mint for missing account 9999 raises AccountNotFoundError; rejects dangling credential owner.; test_deleting_an_account_takes_its_ticket: Merge removes absorbed account and its ORPHAN ticket; lookup fails and ticket table is empty. test_no_lockout_before_the_cap: Records MAX_FAILURES−1 attempts and checks each returns no deadline and read reports unlocked; pins strict threshold boundary.; test_the_cap_starts_a_lockout_and_the_read_agrees: The cap-crossing attempt under fixed nanosecond time returns and persists identical deadline rounded to PostgreSQL microseconds, later than now; no pre-cap case reaches this transition.; test_a_success_clears_the_row: After one fewer than cap failures, clear then spend MAX_FAILURES−1 new attempts without a lockout; confirms successful redemption restores full budget rather than only suppressing current deadline.; test_reaching_the_cap_resets_the_count: Hits lockout cap, clears row, then one failure returns no lockout; specifically validates reset after saturated/capped state, complementing pre-cap clear.; test_the_lockout_is_scoped_to_one_identity: Locks Discord subject, then checks different Discord subject and same subject in Java provider remain unlocked; key includes provider+subject.; test_an_expired_lockout_stops_blocking: Creates negative-duration lockout, reads no active lockout and verifies failures can consume a fresh budget; covers elapsed timestamp handling without wall-clock wait.; test_concurrent_failures_are_all_counted: Runs MAX_FAILURES upserts concurrently and requires exactly one caller to report crossing cap plus an active persisted lock; protects against lost increments.; test_failing_again_while_locked_does_not_report_a_new_lockout: After crossing cap, another failure returns no new deadline and read returns original `started` deadline, so attackers cannot extend lockout by failing again.; test_a_cap_of_one_locks_on_the_first_failure: Calls insert-path upsert with max_failures=1 and verifies first failure creates active lock; ordinary cap test exercises update path after pre-existing row.

test_both_spellings_of_the_consent_gate_agree: Six persisted `(created_at, consent_version)` states straddle cutoff and distinguish never-consented/current/stale receipts; SQL row filtering must agree with Python `consent_refresh_required`. This cross-check prevents authorization/read filters from diverging.

test_issue_persists_one_sorted_array_for_duplicate_unsorted_scopes: Issues `vote.poll.cast`, whitespace-padded build read, and duplicate vote scope, then queries the stored PostgreSQL array and requires sorted unique canonical values. Covers normalization at the persistence service boundary; owner authority and rollback are tested in the UOW file.

test_issuance_checks_current_authority_despite_a_cached_grant: Grant owner `build.submission.approve`, warm cache, issue once, revoke in DB without invalidating local cache, then issuance must be denied and leave exactly one key. The already issued token still authenticates and records first use; a second use within throttle interval preserves prior timestamp/IP. Combines current-authority transaction check with usage write throttling, distinct from scope normalization.; test_failed_commit_rolls_back_the_flushed_key_before_returning_a_secret: A UOW whose commit raises after repository flush must propagate RuntimeError and leave zero ApiKey rows, proving plaintext secret is not returned for a transaction that did not commit.

test_a_backward_page_comes_back_in_display_order: Five confirmed IDs establish descending display order; the test checks an `after_id` slice and a `before_id` slice both return newest-first rows. The other paging tests compare offset/keyset and count traversal, so they do not cover reversal of backward fetch order.; test_an_offset_page_and_a_keyset_page_agree: On the same five rows, offset 2 and the keyset anchor after row 2 must both return rows 3–4. This catches divergent filters/order; the backward-page case covers a different selector branch.; test_the_total_matches_what_paging_actually_returns: Walks five rows two at a time with a third-row sentinel; asserts count=5, no duplicate IDs, and every row is seen once. The other page tests do not validate count against practical cursor traversal.

test_list_page_query_count_does_not_grow_with_the_page: Seeds 1 versus 5 builds with creators, submitter identity, and version, then expects the same eight SELECT budget. This is the page-size/N+1 regression check; `test_get_many_batches_cross_context_loads` covers a different read API.; test_get_many_batches_cross_context_loads: Loads five IDs and checks each creator, version, and Discord submitter plus the same eight-query budget. The page query test only counts a list page and would not catch N+1s or bad grouping in `get_many`.; test_get_builds_by_id_preserves_positions_including_duplicates: Requests `[id0, missing, id1, id0]` and expects the same positional sequence with `None` and duplicate preserved. It protects the positional API contract absent from set-oriented `get_many`.

test_round_trip_is_identity_for_known_taxonomy: For all five build subclasses, `_make_build` supplies the full known field set (all restriction buckets, five link types, creators, version metadata, and category fields); `_assert_round_trip` checks every comparable dataclass field after taxonomy resolution and reload. `test_round_trip_property` uses varied but narrower generated subsets, so does not subsume this broad fixed matrix.; test_attachment_enrichment_evidence_round_trips_as_nested_json: Persists nested duplicate evidence and two attachment failure records with IDs, stages, and explanatory details; exact `extra_info` equality protects these worker-produced JSON structures through ORM JSONB writes.; test_loaded_status_is_a_status_member: Reloaded `submission_status` must be the actual `Status.PENDING` member (the `.name` assertion catches bare integer despite IntEnum equality); then repository confirmation must reload as `Status.CONFIRMED`. This tests enum conversion in both directions. The `.name == "PENDING"` assertion is implied once identity with `Status.PENDING` succeeds; it is harmless documentation but could be dropped if reducing redundant assertions.; test_persisting_a_build_creates_no_account: Records account count before saving a build for an existing owner, then checks neither accounts nor identities were created. It protects separation of build persistence from account provisioning.; test_persisting_a_build_for_an_unknown_account_is_refused: A build with nonexistent submitter 999999 raises `InvalidStateError`; the repository must not silently manufacture an account or accept dangling ownership. Existing-account persistence above covers the valid side.; test_update_round_trip_preserves_category_fields: Parameterized across categories, edits common fields and door dimensions/timing or extender length/timing, saves/reloads, then checks every comparable dataclass field. Initial insert round-trip does not cover detached update mapping.; test_alias_resolves_to_canonical_display_name: An official alias `No Observers` is rewritten to canonical `Observerless` during taxonomy preparation and remains canonical after DB load; ambiguous alias handling is separate below.; test_source_messages_round_trip: Two submitted MessageSnapshots with IDs, author/content/time, guild/channel round-trip to ordered MessageRefs; first original link stays the initial request and message details persist. The later one-message/two-build case checks multiplicity, not snapshot ingestion/order.; test_saving_a_build_keeps_newer_source_message_content: After loading a build, records a newer Discord message edit, then saves the stale build copy; message content must remain `edited` while build description changes. The single-match alias case above is not equivalent.; test_save_persists_tags_verbatim_without_mutating_input: A raw repository save of a door with empty patterns must leave `patterns` and `tags` empty both in memory and after reload; it proves taxonomy defaults belong to preparation, not persistence.; test_apply_build_taxonomy_defaults_door_pattern: Calling taxonomy preparation on an empty-pattern door supplies visible `Regular` plus the stable `pattern-regular` assignment before save; this complements the raw-save test by pinning the application transformation.; test_replacing_links_of_one_media_type_moves_a_shared_url: Assigns one URL as image then video, clears images, and reloads video-only. This asserts the `(build,url)` unique row is reclassified instead of duplicated or deleted.; test_an_unknown_door_size_stays_unknown_through_save_and_reload: Persists a historical DoorBuild with all door dimensions `None`; reload must keep all unknown rather than substitute a default. The round-trip fixtures have concrete dimensions and cannot cover this null edge.; test_round_trip_property: Hypothesis generates up to 12 persisted builds with random sparse dimensions, descriptions, creator lists, image/video links, taxonomy lists, and category-specific facts; fieldwise reload catches combinations the fixed fully populated fixture misses. The fixed fixture remains for fields this strategy omits (e.g. version spec, completion evidence, all restriction/link buckets).; test_repeat_credit_of_a_case_folding_name_resolves_to_one_alias: Three build credits `ΣΣ`, `ΣΣ`, `Σς` must create exactly one normalized creator alias `σσ`; it protects the casefold lookup-before-insert path that per-name folding and simple conflict tests do not integrate with build save.; test_detached_build_preview_changes_only_on_explicit_save: Mutates nested extra_info, links and tag evidence on a loaded copy; the original and DB remain unchanged until save, then changes persist and revision increments once. This exercises detached aggregate copies and nested relationships beyond simple reload.; test_source_read_preserves_unclassified_links: Loads a source-submission build containing a link with `media_type=None` via the specialized source read and asserts session remains clean and row stays unclassified; ordinary `get_by_id` round-trip does not exercise this read path's no-autoflush behavior.; test_tracked_status_change_advances_the_revision_once: Within editing scope calls repository `confirm`, then confirms status and exactly one revision increment after reload; the prior status mapping test checks enum values but not trigger revision accounting.; test_showcase_tags_are_replaced_by_key_beside_resolved_restrictions: Replaces showcase assignment with `compact` on a loaded utility build, then checks the key and preexisting restrictions survive. This is a relationship update contract not covered by ordinary restriction round-trips. Decisions: removed redundant assertion test_loaded_status_is_a_status_member: Enum identity already proves its name; removed name assertion only.

test_snapshot_reuse_pagination_and_final_state: Two commits mutate description twice in one scope; asserts three history entries share adjacent snapshots, no pending edits remain, cursor round-trip returns the same first item, and `second`→`third` states are stored. The direct-write, rollback, and concurrency cases below each cover separate trigger/transaction behavior.; test_unscoped_writes_are_rejected: Parameterized raw UPDATE build, INSERT link, and DELETE build outside scope each must raise the named DB trigger error; proves all three tracked write families are fenced, beyond repository-only calls.; test_scope_closes_flushes_and_does_not_leak: A scoped mutation flushes on exit and persists; a later UPDATE without scope fails, and a second scope in the same transaction fails. This catches both premature scope teardown and context leakage.; test_noops_bookkeeping_rollback_and_direct_sql: In one scenario transient→original writes coalesce, a failed ORM save rolls back, and later direct link+description SQL creates one history snapshot with links. It exercises trigger net-change/bookkeeping and exception rollback, unlike simple snapshot equality.; test_immutability: Parameterized UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE against both history tables must fail with `append-only`; protects database-enforced audit retention, not a Python repository convention.; test_concurrent_edits_record_only_the_winner: Two detached copies with the same revision race; exactly one saves and one gets stale, leaving only initial+winner history entries. Only a real PostgreSQL row lock/revision check can establish this.; test_merge_and_delete_retain_history: Merges submitter ownership then deletes the build inside attributed scopes; history keeps both merge and delete records and orders delete first. No other test covers history retention across account merge/deletion.; test_migration_preserves_history: Downgrades to a pre-history revision and upgrades; a preexisting build's history remains available. Migration preservation is distinct from runtime history behavior.; test_writes_after_scope_exit_roll_back_the_transaction: A post-scope raw write fails and explicit rollback leaves description `first` and only the original history row. This checks the transaction is not left partially dirty after guard rejection.; test_savepoint_rollback_keeps_only_surviving_changes: Inside one edit scope, a nested update is rolled back to a savepoint and a later update survives; the single history entry records `first`→`survived`, not `discarded`. It covers PostgreSQL trigger behavior under savepoints.

test_repository_round_trips_and_updates_every_manifest_category: Persists and reloads each of five categories with account ownership, source draft lookup, pending listing and per-account paging; updates every category and checks revision 2; duplicate draft source violates the unique constraint. Unlike taxonomy-rich round-trip tests, this pins submission-specific fields and repository listing/index paths.; test_repository_round_trips_immutable_public_sponsor_snapshot: Saves a `PublicSponsor` and reads both domain projection and exact sponsor columns, including installation UUID/address/site. The later merge tests preserve owner references but do not assert immutable sponsor value mapping.; test_public_summaries_select_only_allowlisted_fields_and_preserve_requested_order: Queries confirmed+pending IDs with a duplicate, absent ID, private description/provenance, and render/video links; result contains duplicate confirmed summary in request order with display name/render preview. This public projection guards filtering and data minimization not full Build loading.; test_submission_target_persists_only_the_exact_canonical_source_version: Accepts exact `Java 1.21.0`, maps unknown `Java 1.21.99` to stable attention with no target row, and direct invalid repository write raises without insert. These cover adapter classification and persistence validation as separate boundaries.; test_concurrent_source_draft_writes_publish_and_materialize_one_submission_event: Runs two finalization executions for one claimed draft; exactly one returns the finalized build, one source-key build/event is stored, and replayed notification materialization yields one staff notification. Exercises DB uniqueness and downstream event idempotency under a real race.; test_notification_materialize_merge_and_replay_coalesces_recipient_state: Creates duplicate staff notifications/deliveries for survivor+absorbed accounts, marks one read and one sent, merges, retries stale delivery and rematerializes; requires one survivor row preserving read/sent timestamps while clearing claims. Different from no-collision merge and late-integrity rollback cases.; test_account_merge_transfers_submission_and_minecraft_authorization_ownership: A single merge moves build/draft/access/change actor/schematic rights, Paper installation, approved challenge, grant, and Java identity to survivor while preserving installation ID/hash and removing absorbed account. Broad reference graph regression complements focused payload/digest merge tests below.; test_account_merge_rewrites_pending_payloads_and_fences_claimed_work: Seeds one pending and one claimed Paper finalization with sponsor, merges owner, verifies execution payload owner+digest rewritten while immutable original input still names absorbed account, stale claim rejected/reclaimed, and immutable input UPDATE rejected. `test_account_merge_refuses_to_bless_a_conflicting_finalization_digest` tests rollback when the starting digest is already corrupt.; test_account_merge_refuses_to_bless_a_conflicting_finalization_digest: Corrupts a queued payload digest before account merge; merge must raise integrity error and preserve absorbed account, draft owner and corrupt bytes. Complements the valid-digest rewrite case by ensuring a migration cannot launder corrupted retained work.; test_account_merge_carries_permission_rules_and_keeps_the_stricter_effect: Merges overlapping allow/forbid grant, duplicate built-in assignments, custom role/audit authorship; verifies forbid wins and every account reference points to survivor. The test isolates permission collision policy from generic FK moves.; test_imported_door_with_unknown_facts_commits_and_reloads: Runs the production submission preparation/executor with a Discord payload lacking source version, dimensions, orientation and creators; persisted result is a DoorBuild retaining `(None,3,None)`, None orientation, empty creators/versions. The build model null test skips submission conversion and provenance rules.

test_enrollment_secrets_are_hash_only_and_exchange_is_one_time: Completes Ed25519 enrollment using device code proof after browser approval; authenticates resulting token, rejects second exchange, and checks device-code, user-code and session-token plaintext do not occur in stored digests. The later challenge-renewal case tests device lifecycle after issuance, not initial exchange secrecy.; test_signed_nonce_renews_session_and_device_revocation_fences_both: Signs one fresh device/challenge/nonce proof to renew session, authenticates the new token, revokes the device as its owner, then asserts both original and renewed tokens fail. Covers one-time renewal and all-session revocation, beyond initial enrollment exchange.

test_a_delivery_is_claimed_with_its_event_and_acknowledged: Claim returns joined event/consumer/token; completion deletes delivery but retains event log row. Covers durable log versus per-consumer queue semantics.; test_another_consumer_does_not_see_this_consumers_deliveries: Discord delivery is invisible to webhooks claim and visible to Discord; checks consumer-scoped queue predicate.; test_a_stale_delivery_token_cannot_acknowledge: Clears current claim in DB then stale token completion returns false and row remains; verifies token fence on acknowledgement.; test_a_failed_delivery_backs_off_and_a_ceiling_failure_dead_letters_it: Failure one schedules backoff/increments attempt; retry at attempt ceiling dead-letters, clears claim and records error, then disappears from claim results.

test_confirming_a_build_emits_one_event_with_a_delivery_per_consumer: Build pending→confirmed emits submitted and confirmed transitions, one delivery per consumer, schema v3 payload and first_confirmation/submitter fields; covers event fanout and payload evolution.; test_denying_a_build_emits_a_denied_event: Pending→denied trigger emits submitted plus denied event; distinct terminal transition branch from confirmed event.; test_rewriting_the_same_status_emits_nothing: Starts confirmed and writes same status; trigger must compare OLD/NEW and avoid duplicate event on idempotent update.; test_returning_a_build_to_pending_emits_nothing: Confirmed→pending is a real status change but not a terminal event, so only insert-time submitted event remains; checks unsupported transition branch.; test_inserting_a_build_emits_a_submitted_event: Insert-time trigger emits submitted event even when starting status is confirmed; keeps initial creation branch distinct from update transition.; test_closing_a_vote_session_emits_one_event: Open→closed plus repeated closed write produces one vote_session.closed with kind/result payload; exercises vote trigger transition and duplicate suppression.; test_no_registered_consumers_records_the_event_without_deliveries: With consumer table empty, build transitions still persist both event log records but no deliveries; separates durable event log from fanout audience.; test_publisher_records_the_schema_version: Calls production publish_domain_event directly with version 2/custom envelope and confirms all stored fields; trigger defaults alone would not exercise publisher parameter contract.

test_listener_delivers_commit_hints_reconnects_and_closes_on_cancellation: Runs real PostgreSQL LISTEN connection, confirms startup wake, no hint before transaction commit, receives committed NOTIFY, kills backend and verifies reconnect/new PID, then cancellation closes backend.

test_version_service_honors_explicit_edition: Calls VersionService.add("1.21.4", edition="Bedrock") and checks both the returned value and committed repository row use Bedrock. `test_parse_version_string` covers parsed edition/default patch only; it cannot catch the application override or commit path.; test_version_service_lists_both_editions: Seeds Java and Bedrock rows and asserts list_all returns both in repository order. `test_version_service_resolves_ranges_and_newest_version` does not exercise list_all or its two edition reads.; test_version_service_resolves_ranges_and_newest_version: Checks newest selects the final catalog entry and resolves a mixed inclusive range plus `+` across patch entries. `test_version_ranges_accept_message_separators` only checks alternate range separators and different bounds; it does not cover newest, range expansion, or plus selection.; test_version_service_reports_an_empty_catalog_as_infrastructure_failure: Requires newest on an empty edition to raise VersionCatalogUnavailableError with edition context.
